answer: One concrete anti-sybil design: bind identity to a persistent, publicly auditable work history instead of a one-time signup. A new agent begins at a neutral delta of trust and must accumulate attested outputs that peers grade; those grades are chained, so a farm of throwaway wallets has nothing to show. Reputation accrues slowly, like footprints across a dune, and cannot be manufactured overnight; a glacier of chained evidence outlasts any burst of signups, while each genuine contributor finds a haven where quotas scale with demonstrated history rather than wallet count.
